title: Parallel and Intersecting Lines: Angles and Transversals
seo_title: Parallel and Intersecting Lines Class 7 Worksheet with Answers (Ganita Prakash Part 1, Chapter 5)
standard_code: Class 7, Ganita Prakash Part 1, Chapter 5: Parallel and Intersecting Lines
standard_text: Intersecting lines, linear pairs and vertically opposite angles; parallel lines and transversals; corresponding, alternate and interior angles; checking for parallel lines (summary of NCERT Ganita Prakash Class 7)
meta_desc: Class 7 Parallel and Intersecting Lines worksheet (Ganita Prakash Part 1, Chapter 5): vertically opposite angles, linear pairs, corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Corresponding and alternate angles are equal
key_sub: Interior angles on the same side add up to 180°.
body_html:
How it works

When two lines cross, vertically opposite angles are equal and angles next to each other form a linear pair (add up to 180°).

A transversal crossing two parallel lines makes equal corresponding angles (same position, F-shape) and equal alternate angles (Z-shape). Interior angles on the same side (C-shape) add up to 180°.

Example

Two lines cross; one angle is 65°. Find the angle next to it.

Linear pair: 180° − 65°

Answer: 115°

Example

Alternate angles on parallel lines: one is 48°. Find the other.

Alternate angles are equal

Answer: 48°

Common mistakes

  • Taking corresponding angles as supplementary.
  • Taking interior angles on the same side as equal.
  • Using 90° for a linear pair instead of 180°.

faq.a: The opposite angles formed when two lines cross. They are always equal.

faq.q: What angles are formed when a transversal cuts two parallel lines?
faq.a: Corresponding angles (equal), alternate angles (equal) and interior angles on the same side (add up to 180°).

faq.q: How can you check whether two lines are parallel?
faq.a: If a transversal makes equal corresponding or alternate angles, the lines are parallel.

sets.title: Algebra and checking for parallel lines

items.q: A line crosses two other lines. A pair of alternate angles measure 60° and 65°. Are the two lines parallel?
c: Yes, because the angles are close
No, because all angles must be 90°
You cannot tell without measuring the lines
No, because the alternate angles are not equal
items.e: For parallel lines, corresponding and alternate angles are equal and co-interior angles add to 180°. Here 60° and 65° are different, so no.

items.q: Corresponding angles between parallel lines are 5x and 70°. Find x.
items.e: Corresponding angles are equal: 5x = 70, so x = 14°.
